land.text: the Principality of Catalonia with Roussillon: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and most of Tarragona, and the north now in the Pyrénées-Orientales

predecessors.note: The Principality was part of the Spanish crowns inside the Iberian Union (Cliopatria's row to 1639); the kingdom-of-spain dossier names Spain as the other party of the 1640 contest.

land.text: Catalonia under the protection of Louis XIII, recognised as Count of Barcelona

successors.note: A French protectorate from January 1641: the kingdom-of-france dossier records the vassal relation 1641-1652 (vassal_start 1641, vassal_end 1652); Spain recaptured Barcelona in 1652 and France kept Roussillon until the Treaty of the Pyrenees (1659).

capitals.name: Barcelona
capitals.note: 'The capital and largest city, Barcelona'; the Bloody Corpus rising took place in Barcelona (Reapers' War page).

rulers.name: Pau Claris (president of the Generalitat)
rulers.title: president of the Generalitat
rulers.note: The page: president of the Generalitat, elected in 1638; he 'died a month later' after the Battle of Montjuïc, 'probably poisoned by Spanish agents'. It does not call him head of the Republic.

rulers.name: Louis XIII of France (as Count of Barcelona, Louis I)
rulers.title: Count of Barcelona
rulers.note: Recognised by Claris's appeal of 23 January 1641; the Franco-Spanish War page: 'the Catalan Courts recognised Louis XIII as Count of Barcelona'.

keyframe_review.note: 33,801 km2 against the infobox 32,113.86 km2 of modern Catalonia on the Catalonia page (ratio 1.05, well inside a factor of two). The shape is Barcelona, Gerona and Lérida provinces, 69 percent of Tarragona province (the Tortosa end is outside) and 95 percent of the Pyrénées-Orientales (Roussillon): the Catalonia page says 'Modern-day Catalonia comprises most of the medieval and early modern Principality of Catalonia, with the remainder of the northern area now part of France's Pyrénées-Orientales', and the Reapers' War page has the Treaty of the Pyrenees cede 'the County of Roussillon and the northern half of the County of Cerdanya'. The pages do not say which fortresses stayed Spanish in 1640-1641 (they name only later sieges of Tarragona, Lleida and Tortosa that 'finally failed'), so the shape is taken as the whole Principality; unverified in detail.

ledger.note: 1640: Barcelona rises in the Bloody Corpus and the Principality of Catalonia is in revolt against Philip IV. The page: the uprising occurred on 'the Corpus Christi day of May 1640' in Barcelona and the viceroy, the second Count of Santa Coloma, 'was assassinated'; no day is given. The Principality's land is the researcher's reading from the Catalonia page.

region.text: the Principality of Catalonia with Roussillon: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and most of Tarragona, and the north now in the Pyrénées-Orientales

ledger.note: 1640: the Reapers' War begins between the Principality and the Spanish Crown. Counterpart as in the kingdom-of-spain dossier (its contest_start catalonia, 1640); the Crown's rule was held by the Iberian Union until 1 December 1640. The Catalonia page dates the war '(1640-1652)'.

region.text: the Principality of Catalonia with Roussillon: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and most of Tarragona, and the north now in the Pyrénées-Orientales

ledger.note: 17 January 1641: the Catalan Republic is proclaimed under French protection. 'On 17 January 1641, the Junta de Braços accepted the establishment of the Catalan Republic under French protection.' The Catalonia page: 'briefly as a republic led by the president of the Generalitat, Pau Claris'.

January 1641 (closing the pair, confidence 1): the independent Catalan state ends, but the war with Spain goes on under French protection; the page has Spain capture Barcelona only in 1652 ('the French authorities renounced Catalonia, but held control of Roussillon'). The contest continues in the kingdom-of-spain and kingdom-of-france dossiers.

region.text: the Principality of Catalonia with Roussillon: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and most of Tarragona, and the north now in the Pyrénées-Orientales

ledger.note: 23 January 1641: Catalonia accepts Louis XIII. Pau Claris 'appealed on 23 January 1641 to Louis XIII, recognizing him as Count of Barcelona'; the Franco-Spanish War page: 'In 1641, the Catalan Courts recognised Louis XIII as Count of Barcelona.' The Battle of Montjuïc, 'fought on 26 January 1641', was won by the Franco-Catalan armies. Cliopatria's row runs to the end of 1641; the kingdom-of-france dossier carries the protectorate 1641-1652.

region.text: the Catalan Republic and Roussillon, now under Louis XIII

wars.name: Reapers' War

zones.text: the Principality of Catalonia with Roussillon: the provinces of Barcelona, Gerona, Lerida and most of Tarragona, and the north now in the Pyrénées-Orientales

wars.outcome: Infobox: 'Revolt suppressed by Spain'. Catalan Republic under French protection (17 January 1641), Franco-Catalan victory at Montjuïc (26 January 1641), Spanish recapture of Barcelona in 1652; Roussillon and the northern half of Cerdanya ceded to France in 1659.
wars.note: This dossier covers the independent Catalan state (May 1640 to January 1641) only; the page gives no capital for the Republic.

wars.name: Franco-Spanish War (1635-1659)
wars.outcome: Stalemate 1637-1659; the Treaty of the Pyrenees (5 or 7 November 1659, the page gives both) gives France Artois, Hainaut towns and Roussillon; Louis XIV 'renounced his claim to be Count of Barcelona and King of Catalonia'.
wars.note: The page says that 'in 1640 erupted into open revolts in Portugal and Catalonia'.

certainty.note: The Principality's frontier with Aragon and the Tortosa end of Tarragona province are Cliopatria approximations; the Pyrenean frontier with France is the Roussillon-Cerdanya line the Treaty of the Pyrenees only moved in 1659.

notes:
Catalonia (Cliopatria 1640-1641), a one-row state. Pages: Reapers' War, Catalonia (budget 1-2) plus the Franco-Spanish War page, which was opened for the iberian-union dossier.

Type: rebel (the Principality in revolt, then a republic under French protection for days). The kingdom-of-france dossier carries Catalonia as a vassal 1641-1652; this dossier ends in January 1641 so the two do not double-draw after the first weeks of 1641, though Cliopatria's row runs to the end of 1641 (the compiler should let the France vassal drawing win in 1641 after January).

Not settled: (1) the month of the Bloody Corpus: the Reapers' War page says 'the Corpus Christi day of May 1640' and gives no day; I used month 5 as the page does. (2) Which fortresses and towns stayed Spanish in 1640-1641 (Tortosa, Salses and others): the pages name only later sieges. (3) The year Roussillon's Perpignan fell to France: the Reapers' War page says 'Perpignan was taken from the Spanish after a siege of 10 months' without a year (the kingdom-of-france dossier has 1642). (4) The page gives no capital for the Republic; Barcelona is taken from the Catalonia page and the site of the uprising. (5) Predecessor: I name iberian-union (the Cliopatria row in 1639), while the kingdom-of-spain dossier names itself as the other party of the contest; both are consistent with the union's split on 1 December 1640.
